title: A smooth three-torus diffeomorphism with simple Lebesgue spectrum
main_claim: There is a C^infty volume-preserving diffeomorphism T of T^3 and a real f in L^2_0 such that {f∘T^n} is an orthonormal basis of L^2_0. So U_T has simple Lebesgue spectrum on the whole centered space, and T is mixing, has zero entropy and has zero Lyapunov exponents.
coverage:
I read all six sections in full. Checks I did myself:
(1) Passage lemma. Conjugation C_N T_N C_N^{-1} = twist with speed sigma_N, checked by direct substitution. C^k convergence T_N -> S, including the derivatives in a and the N V^{(k)} terms. Stationary-phase amplitude |C|^2 ≈ W/N, consistent with total mass ∫|A|^2. Fine-density formula K(j/N, Nt-j) and its fast-variable average giving back the old density.
(2) Signal lemma. Fourier moments of s·J_* with J_*=(R/B+h/P)/c. The character sum gives the indicator that gcd(lm,P)=1. The sieve argument (l ≤ D/b < L means a prime factor of l divides P) kills the l ≥ 2 moments. The baseline term vanishes since alpha < tau·b. Q_h stays positive under the stated gamma_0. The finite-c error bound holds.
(3) Neutral refresh. Riemann-sum error ||∂_a f_s||_1/(|s|L) for residue equalization. Refresh-transmit error bookkeeping, including lambda = gamma·phi(P)/P.
(4) Prediction proposition. E H_r = 1. E H_r H_s = (1+2 lambda^2 Re(a_r conj(a_s)))^n. The linear terms sum to 2n lambda^2 |beta-q|^2. Remainder ≤ 162 e^{18 delta} delta^2. The square-root inequality has the identity (t-1)^2(t^2+2t+1/2). Under H_r: E Z_i = lambda a_r and E|Z_i - lambda a_r|^2 = 1 - lambda^2|a_r|^2, so the cross term vanishes pointwise. Error propagation E_i ≤ M E_{i-1} + eta_i. The phase-test lemma's coefficients are fixed before the L_i are chosen. Telescoping gives Hellinger loss 400 K delta^2 and prediction error 5/(K delta), and K = ceil(10/(eps^2 delta)) makes both work.
(5) Stage proposition. Angular averages are converted to nonzero modes by two passages. The ratio and tagging step via F+tH. The flat vector has density 1/2+1/2. Whitening distance ∫(sqrt p - 1)^2, and G = (sqrt p)(U) f'. Diagonal limit: strong Koopman continuity gives orthonormality of the limit orbit and keeps the polynomial approximations. The density-norm bound is applied only at a fixed map.
Corollaries: Riemann–Lebesgue gives mixing. Rokhlin's finite-multiplicity theorem gives zero entropy. Pesin's formula plus volume preservation gives zero exponents. These are standard.
Limits of the check: I did not re-derive every o(1) uniformity in stationary phase (the tail bound O(N^{-1/2}/D), the integration-by-parts tails) beyond spot checks.
sibling_notes: The family 144 board was empty when I started. The only companion dependence is MultipleMixing2026, and it is used only for mixing of all orders in the corollary. The main theorem does not depend on it, so there is no circularity.
